title: Self-Dual Lattice Function
body_html:
Self-Dual Lattice Function

Let \(V\) carry a nondegenerate sesquilinear form. For an \(o_D\)-lattice \(L\subseteq V\), its dual is \[ L^\#=\{v\in V : \langle v,L\rangle_V\subseteq \mathfrak p_D\}. \] This knowledge base uses the conductor-\(\mathfrak p\) convention for the fixed additive character \(\psi\). Some sources denote the same dual lattice by \(L^\ast\); the notation \(L^\vee\) is avoided here.

For a lattice function \(L\), the dual lattice function is defined by \[ (L^\#)_s=(L_{(-s)+})^\#. \] The lattice function is self-dual when \(L=L^\#\). Under the Bruhat-Tits identification for classical groups, points in the building correspond to self-dual lattice functions.
